$source: the product's own first rule about numbers: quote a figure with the conditions it was measured under and with whose it is, or do not quote it
$rule: One register of figures with the conditions each was measured under and whose it is, read by two checks. scripts/policy-sentences.py in this repository holds every figure on a shipped surface that is answered by its conditions to an entry here, and to the entry's saidWith phrase where it has one. scripts/figures-stated.mjs in the site repository holds every figure with a time unit on a served page to an entry here marked servedOnSite. A number that is not here is refused by both rather than shipping. From 2026-09-17 an entry also says what its figure is of, one of $subjects, and a sentence naming the figure as something else is refused; an entry marked superseded is refused where a sentence says it has not been replaced or quotes it as today's. From the afternoon of 2026-09-17 every entry, whatever its whose says, names evidence that carries the figure and that the check can read: a receipt in this repository whose field for the entry's subject is the figure, a file in this repository that states the figure, or, for a figure that is somebody else's, the document it is quoted from; an entry of a measurement names its owner, the machine and the path, from $owners, and a sentence giving it another is refused; an entry marked constant is refused where a sentence calls it measured; an entry marked history or superseded is refused where a sentence says it in the present.
$written: 2026-09-10, in the site repository. Before it, the front page carried a made-up 12.4 ms with the conditions of a public research figure attached, and nothing would have told anybody so. Moved into this repository on 2026-09-16, so that the check on the site and the check on this repository's own surfaces read one register rather than two, and extended with every figure this repository's surfaces quote.

$subjects.$rule: What a figure in this register is of, and the words a sentence may use to say so. Every entry names one. A sentence quoting a figure is read for the nearest of these words to it in its own clause, the one directly after it ("35.081 ms of the sources overlapping") first and otherwise the nearest before it ("the residual falls from 13.522 ms"), and that word has to be one the entry's subject is named by. A sentence that names no subject near the figure is not held to one, because a list of readings names what they are once, at its head. A subject named by nothing is not held to this at all: it is a setting, a condition or an illustration, and a sentence about it can call it anything but a measured part of a bound. The words under neutral are read past. Each measured subject names the receipt field it is read off, so an entry whose evidence is a receipt is held to that field and to nothing else in the receipt.

the whole interval.what: the whole width of an interval, a receipt or a reading

half the committed receipt.what: half the width of the committed receipt, either side of the reading

the sources overlapping.what: the sources overlapping, one part of a width breakdown

the model's residual.what: the model's own residual, one part of a width breakdown

the oscillator.what: the oscillator since the last exchange, one part of a width breakdown

the widest round trip.what: the widest source round trip halved, reported beside a breakdown

the local read.what: the local read, one part of a width breakdown

the safety margin.what: the fixed safety margin, one part of a width breakdown

the outside signatures gap.what: the gap two outside signatures enclose on a receipt

a ceiling.what: a ceiling a policy or a verifier sets, a setting rather than a measurement

a setting or a condition.what: a setting, a condition a measurement was taken at, an interface fixture or an illustration

a time to answer.what: how long the agent took to answer a caller

$owners.$rule: Whose a measured figure is, on two axes: the machine it was taken on and the path it was taken through. Every entry of a measurement names both. A sentence quoting the figure is read, in the figure's own clause, for the words naming each owner, and a word naming another owner on either axis refuses it, naming the entry, the word and the owner. Until 2026-09-17 the three most quoted figures, the committed receipt's, the agent's and the runner's, could be swapped between a desktop and a runner and between the agent and the one-shot command on every surface.
